You will define these systems, build them with our manufacturing team, and own them through their life: maintenance, upgrades to each programme baseline, and availability to the teams that depend on them. This is a build-from-scratch role with budget and rack space already allocated. You will also act as our test architect: we have deep physics and engineering expertise, and you will bring the formal software-testing experience to shape what gets tested where (simulation versus real hardware) and how testing gates releases. You will start with one engineer hire alongside you and grow the team deliberately, turning the test estate into a reliable service the engineering teams depend on. jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
jobs.description_text: Role At Oxford Ionics, now part of IonQ, we are building the first practical quantum computer. Our systems are based on ion traps, which hold individual atomic ions tens of microns above the surface of a chip, and we design and build them in house, bringing together optomechanics, vacuum and cryogenic technology, electronics and system infrastructure. We are looking for a Senior Mechanical Engineer to join our Systems team and take ownership of mechanical design from first requirements through to manufacture and integration. You will work on the hardware that surrounds the quantum processor, including cryostat requirements, cooling equipment, vacuum chambers and supporting structures, often in areas where the requirements are not yet fully defined. Responsibilities: You will work alongside scientists, technicians and the wider hardware design teams to bring new systems through to manufacture. That means producing CAD designs, bills of materials and assembly drawings, managing documentation in our PLM system and working with suppliers and our manufacturing team. Our manufacturing team handles most assembly, but you will support technicians in the lab, investigate problems when they arise and make sure your designs can be built in practice. The work ranges from complex system layout to simple brackets and documentation, and you will see each piece through to completion. You will keep the product lifecycle management (PLM) system, build records and engineering change requests (ECRs) up to date so fixes carry into future builds. About the Role Newton ships on a sprint cadence through a develop, stage and customer-environment pipeline, and the product surface is wide: conversations, blueprints, connectors, scheduled tasks, permissions and sharing, SSO, and AI agents whose behavior is not fully deterministic. A missed regression lands in front of a media planner or a customer's security review. We run everything through an AI-first lens, because it is the only way quality scales. If a quality task is repeatable, an agent does it and you supervise; if it takes judgment, that is where you spend your time. The gap this hire fills: evals and skill-change testing. Code changes already have CI and review, including PRs written by Claude. What has no safety net is behavior change: an edit to a skill, a prompt, a tool definition or a model version can silently change what our agents do, and nothing tests that today. You own that layer: curated eval sets, scoring and regression tracking, so any change to how an agent behaves is measured before it ships. Measure the AI: agent output varies run to run, so “correct” is a range you define with evals, rubrics and scoring, not an exact-match assertion. jobs.title: Software Engineer – Database Kernel
jobs.description_text: The Role: The Kernel team builds the storage engine and transaction machinery inside Neo4j. If you join us, you will not be building web APIs or shuffling data between services. Instead, you will be working directly on the database engine itself. Our day-to-day is low-level systems engineering. We write and maintain custom storage engines, the page cache, transaction handling (WAL, ACID guarantees), indexing, and memory management. The code we write determines how fast queries run across billions of nodes and relationships, and how safely data is written when a machine crashes. We are a pragmatic, engineering-led group split between Malmö and London. We read and discuss database papers (VLDB, SIGMOD, and others) to see what ideas are worth pulling into the product. We also run regular “Do What You Want” weeks so everyone has dedicated time to experiment with their own prototypes or tooling improvements. What you will actually be doing: Designing, profiling, and implementing core database features, including storage formats, index structures, and recovery paths. Diagnosing tricky concurrency bugs, race conditions, and lock contention. Performance engineering: profiling CPU, memory allocation, off-heap memory, and disk I/O to improve latency. Reviewing designs and PRs with a heavy focus on correctness, data integrity, and long-term maintainability. Helping decide technical direction and architectural trade-offs as our engine evolves. What we are looking for: Systems programming

As a Sales Development Representative (SDR) on the Auto team, you’ll be the first point of contact for new-car dealerships and dealer groups, and play a critical role in our growth within the automotive vertical. This is a research-driven function where you’ll map dealer group structures, identify the right accounts and the right timing, and open strategic, executive-level conversations that lead to qualified product demonstrations for our Account Executives. You’ll work closely with AEs and CSMs to understand account context, existing integrations and dealership operations, so that every conversation you have is informed, credible and well-timed. If you have automotive industry experience, whether from a dealership, an automotive IT provider or a related automotive technology business, and you’re looking for a genuine pathway into a closing role, this is where it starts. Many of our top-performing Account Executives started as SDRs, including on the Auto team. The role comes with a clear and transparent career pathway into an Account Executive role on the Auto team, with structured coaching and ongoing sales development. The compensation package includes a competitive base salary, superannuation and uncapped commission with accelerators for overachievement. jobs.title: Senior Compensation Manager
jobs.description_text: The Role We are looking to hire a high-performing Senior Compensation Manager to join our team. In this role, you will own the end-to-end compensation program at Podium, including equity and executive compensation, to ultimately help Podium hire and retain the best global talent. As a leader in People Operations, you will also play an active role in influencing organization design and job architecture. What you will be doing: Partner with executives and senior leadership to ensure our compensation program is attracting the right talent and driving the right behaviors and outcomes for the business Oversee annual compensation planning process, including merit cycle, promotions, off-cycle changes, and executive compensation Design and maintain role classification and benchmarking to ensure we remain competitive and aligned to market trends Own our global equity program, including equity pool planning, management, forecasting, and expansion Refresh and maintain Podium’s compensation philosophy across all roles Partner in broader people operations priorities, including job architecture, leveling, and any other relevant projects What you should have: 5+ years of experience in Compensation at a software company Experience building scalable compensation programs in a fast-moving, evolving environment Excellent analytical and quantitative skills, including Google Sheets/Excel Strong understanding of compensation principles (including equity), market trends, and regulatory requirements

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Enterprise AI solutions - Automotive
jobs.description_text: At Podium, our mission is to arm every local business with a complete platform and outcome-driven AI employees that convert leads into real, paying customers. Every day, millions of workers use our AI lead conversion and communication platform to help them get more leads and make more money. Help enterprise automotive groups turn AI into a better way to run their businesses. At Podium, you will lead the team responsible for helping strategic automotive customers deploy AI, change how their teams work, and deliver measurable results across sales and service. You will work directly with dealer group executives and dealership leaders to identify opportunities, build an AI adoption roadmap, and turn that roadmap into operational change across multiple locations. This role combines executive advisory work with people leadership and accountability for customer retention and growth. We are looking for someone who can structure an ambiguous business problem, earn the trust of senior leaders, and stay close to execution. You could come from management consulting, technology transformation, enterprise solutions, or customer success; what matters is your ability to lead teams and deliver business outcomes. What you will do Lead and develop a team serving Podium’s enterprise automotive customers. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - GTM
jobs.description_text: About the Role: We’re looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer who’s excited about AI and thinks like a product owner. Someone who is scrappy, opinionated, and energized by building from zero to one in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. You care more about what ships than what stack you’re shipping on, and you use AI tooling (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) as a genuine force multiplier, not a novelty. At Podium, you’ll have the chance to work on projects that directly shape the success of our platform and the businesses we support. What You Will Be Doing: You'll own features end-to-end, from the first design conversation to production. You'll influence architecture, collaborate closely with product, design and business stakeholders, and help keep our systems reliable as we scale. You'll also invest in the people around you: sharing knowledge, reviewing code, and raising the team's collective ceiling. Contributing to a culture of learning, innovation, and continuous improvement, while staying ahead of trends in AI. What you should have: 7+ years building and shipping production systems, full stack. A track record of owning problems end-to-end, not just executing tickets, but defining and delivering. Strong instincts across the stack: you're comfortable going deep on backend logic, database design, and frontend UX in the same sprint. Fluency with relational databases and search fundamentals. jobs.title: Tech Lead, Site Reliability
jobs.description_text: About the Role We're looking for a SRE Manager to help us build and run infrastructure that just works - even at 3am. You'll lead a team of engineers who care as much about preventing incidents as they do about resolving them, and you'll bring a builder's mindset to reliability: automating toil, sharpening our observability, and increasingly, putting AI to work so humans can focus on the problems that actually need them. This is a role for someone who's equally comfortable in a 1:1 coaching a direct report and in the middle of a SEV-1 driving toward resolution. What you will be doing: Your Team Coach, mentor, and grow a team of SREs — real career development, not just performance reviews on a calendar Hire and retain strong engineers; build a team people want to stay on Create a culture where blameless postmortems are the norm and people feel safe raising issues early Drive day-to-day project management for the team - running standups, grooming and tracking tickets, and keeping work visible to stakeholders Reliability & Systems Own the availability and performance of production systems end-to-end Set the bar on SLIs/SLOs/SLAs and error budgets - and hold the team (and yourself) to them Run incident management: on-call, escalation, and the postmortems that actually change something afterward Push automation hard so the team spends less time on repetitive firefighting and more on durable fixes Own capacity planning, scaling, and disaster recovery strategy AI-Augmented Operation

jobs.title: 2027 Economist Intern
jobs.description_text: A Career with Point72’s Economist Team The Economic and Strategy Research team at Point72 conducts proprietary research on all major economies to support the long/short equity and macro businesses. Its analyses and forecasts inform our portfolio managers’ investment strategies. About the Economist Internship You will join an investment management organization that operates in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. During your time at the firm, you will gain exposure to: Rigorous data compilation and statistical analysis of Asian economies and financial markets Building spreadsheets for economic data relating to Asian countries Contribute to thematic research shared internally with investment teams Using economic data sets and market data platforms for data mining Internship Program at Point72 In addition to the learning and development you’ll receive in your day-to-day role with your team, as a part of our internship program you will: Work alongside your fellow interns and be mentored by experienced professionals Meet your peers through designated intern programming, volunteer opportunities, and social events Attend sessions with senior leaders discussing their expertise and career paths Get hands-on access to the wealth of tools and resources that Point72 employees use everyday Interact with groups and functions with unique responsibilities and perspectives on our industry Develop technical, writing, and presentation skills Participate in networking opportunities across the firm
